I ran `/code-conventions --review-pr` on `d8bd88967...HEAD` (17 files, the Safenet window-coverage and shared-aim changes). I found one real issue, one minor test issue and one out-of-scope note. I changed no tracked files: the full rules checklist was written to my scratchpad instead of `docs/engineering/`.

## Checklist
I went through every rule in `rules.json`. These applied to the diff:

- **Passed:** API-01, FEAT-01, FEAT-03, DATA-02, DATA-06, NUM-02, CODE-06, TEST-02, TEST-03, TEST-04, TEST-05.
- **Flagged:** PROD-01, and a small TEST-01 hygiene issue.
- **Not applicable:** the rest (auth, mobile, CI, transactions, E2E, config, CHAIN, UI tokens and others).

I didn't need to look up the review history behind any rule.

## Findings

**1. PROD-01: a visible copy change with no stated product sign-off (medium)**
`apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/statusPresentation.ts:69` (copy defined at `:49-52`, chosen in `packages/utils/src/features/safenet-checks/hooks/useSafenetCheck.ts:42`)

- **What changes:** before, an empty read in the confirm/execute flow (`SafenetChecksSection`) showed "Not checked · No Safenet check was requested for this transaction." Now any empty read whose window isn't `proven` shows "Status unavailable · The Safenet check status could not be read. Retry later." That covers every head-relative scan, every block estimate that didn't converge, and every transaction older than about 12.5h.
- **Why it's a problem:**
  - Nothing actually failed: the read succeeded.
  - "Retry later" suggests retrying will help. For an old transaction the window will never reach `proven`, so the message stays the same forever.
- **Fix:** get explicit product/design approval for the state change and cite it in the PR, or give `WINDOW_UNCERTAIN` its own neutral copy (e.g. "Check status can't be confirmed for this transaction") instead of reusing the read-failed text.

**2. TEST-01 / test hygiene: fake timers reset only at the end of the test (low)**
`packages/utils/src/features/safenet-checks/hooks/__tests__/useSafenetCheck.test.ts:157-174`

- **What happens:** the new test "anchors the UNAVAILABLE grace window…" calls `jest.useFakeTimers()` and only restores real timers on its last line (`:174`).
- **Why it matters:** if the assertion fails, fake timers leak into later tests. Every other fake-timer block in this file uses `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())` (`:224`, `:271`), so this one is also inconsistent within the diff.
- **Fix:** add an `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())` to the `block window aim` describe block.

**3. Stale comment in a file the diff didn't touch (note)**
`apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/SafenetAuditRow.tsx:37`

- The prop doc still says the timestamp "aims the reader's block window". After this change it's only offered to the aim registry, which keeps the earliest time any surface offered.
- `SafenetQueueStatus.tsx` got the matching comment update; this file didn't. The file is outside the diff, so this is a note, not a finding.

## Open questions
- **PROD-01:** did product/design approve showing "Status unavailable / Retry later" instead of "Not checked" for empty reads that can't be proven?
